signature.name: Palace of the Parliament
signature.detail: The world's heaviest building and a monumental symbol of the communist era, with over 1,000 rooms and opulent interiors. Book a guided tour in advance (passport required) and go early to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Old Town, Bucharest
signature.detail: The historic heart of the city, packed with cobbled streets, 19th-century buildings, and lively cafes and bars. Best explored on foot in the late afternoon or evening when the area comes alive.

signature.name: Romanian Athenaeum
signature.detail: A stunning neoclassical concert hall with a famous domed ceiling and frescoes, home to the George Enescu Philharmonic. Check the schedule for concerts; otherwise visit during the day for a peek at the lobby.

signature.name: Stavropoleos Monastery
signature.detail: A tiny, beautifully carved Orthodox church and monastery tucked away in the Old Town, known for its exquisite frescoes and peaceful courtyard. Dress modestly and visit early morning for quiet reflection.

signature.name: Herastrau Park
signature.detail: Bucharest's largest park, with a lake, gardens, and the open-air Village Museum inside. Rent a boat or bike, and combine with a visit to the museum; go on a weekday for fewer crowds.

signature.name: Village Museum
signature.detail: An open-air museum in Herastrau Park showcasing traditional Romanian rural architecture with original houses and churches. Allow at least two hours; wear comfortable shoes as paths are uneven.

signature.name: Cărturești Carusel
signature.detail: A spectacular bookstore in a restored 19th-century building, often called the most beautiful in Europe. It's free to enter; visit on a weekday morning to avoid the Instagram crowds.

signature.name: Revolution Square
signature.detail: The site of the 1989 revolution that ended communism, surrounded by important buildings like the former Royal Palace. Combine with a visit to the National Museum of Art nearby.

transport: Metro $0.60 a ride; taxis and rideshares cheap
